Categories.value: Daria Daulat Bagh|Self-published work|Uploaded via Campaign:wlm-in|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2020|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments missing SDC depicts|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments missing SDC location of creation|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2020 in India|Files from competitions organized by West Bengal Wikimedians User Group|Images from WLM 2020 India under review by Montage tool

ImageDescription.value: The wooden ceilings are pasted with canvas and painted with floral patterns at Daria Daulat Bagh. It is a palace situated in the city of Srirangapatna, near Mysore, Karnataka. It is mostly made out of teakwood. All of the space available on the walls, pillars, canopies, and arches have colorful frescoes in the style of Mysore paintings. The outer walls of the palace have frescoes of the battle scenes and portraits. The inner walls are decorated with scrolls of thin foliage and floral patterns.

Artist.value: Shashank Mehendale

ImageDescription.value: Daria Daulat Bagh, literally means 'Garden of the Sea of Wealth', is a palace situated in the city of Srirangapatna, Karnataka, India, Tippu Sultan popularly known as the "Tiger of Mysore", built this palace in 1784 and ruled Mysore from here for a short time after his father Hyder Ali wrested power from the Wodeyars in the middle of the 18th century, the palace is built in the Indo-Saracenic style and is mostly made of teakwood, all of the space available on the walls, pillars, canopies and arches have colorful frescoes in the style of Mysore paintings.

ImageDescription.value: The Summer Palace of Tipu Sultan, this was built in 1784. A wooden palace set amongst splendid gardens and flower beds it also features exquisite paintings along the elaborate interiors of the palace. There are beautiful paintings of Haider Ali and Tippu Sultan in battle on the inside walls of this monument. This magnificent structure is raised on a 5-foot tall platform, the top floor here houses the Tipu Sultan Museum which exhibits many of the ruler's belongings along with many European and Persian paintings and manuscripts.
